Title: Seattle Central Library
Note: Rem Koolhaas built it. Take the escalator to the Books Spiral, look up, and stay all afternoon. Free.

Title: Elliott Bay Book Company
Note: Capitol Hill. Wooden floors, a cafe at the back, and no one will hurry you.

Title: Volunteer Park
Note: The Conservatory, the water tower, the art museum and a lot of grass. Capitol Hill's front garden.

Title: Cal Anderson Park
Note: The one everyone ends up at. Shade, a reflecting pool, and a permanent low-grade party in summer.

Title: Optimism Brewing Company
Note: A hall the size of an aircraft hangar with long communal tables. Nobody minds if you nurse one drink.

Title: Ballard Farmers Market
Note: Sundays, year round, rain included. The most reliable way to spend a morning around other people.

Title: Waterfall Garden Park
Note: A hidden courtyard in Pioneer Square with a 22-foot waterfall. Twenty seconds off the street and silent.

Title: Hugo House
Note: A writing centre with a cafe and a reading calendar. Somewhere to go alone on purpose.
